summary: All 63 playable phrases and all 195 four-example sets use basic literal wording. No remaining editorial change is required before export. Each phrase was assessed as the one displayed starter, not by combining a country’s four example facts. This refresh confirms unchanged wording and example sets under the stronger declared-possible-answer policy.
independenceLimitation: I drafted part of the geographic candidate bank and helped revise some wording. This report is a player/editorial assessment, not independent certification of my geographic facts, completeness of memberships, source provenance or fairness bounds. Other current accuracy/fairness review reports were not read to form this verdict.

scope.selectionContext: The candidate selector draws from all eligible alternatives, with name/numeric/geography family weights of 25%/25%/50%. Every hint requires at least four confirmed matches and at least 4/7/7 declared possible matches at Easy/Medium/Hard, with declared possible matches at most 70% of the answer pool. The selector rechecks these bounds against current exclusions. Help says one starter remains stable throughout the round. The four examples are review cards, not the only gameplay choices.

resolvedEditorialIssues.issue: Opaque slogans and rejected letter puzzles
resolvedEditorialIssues.result: No slogan, first/last alphabet-order comparison, or repeated-letter puzzle remains. Alphabet-half clues are retained as explicitly requested.
The ambiguous neighbour-location phrases are absent from the playable catalog.

resolvedEditorialIssues.issue: Indian Ocean umbrella for marginal seas
resolvedEditorialIssues.result: The umbrella phrase is absent. Existing named-sea clues and the simple sea-coast/three-neighbour conjunction provide clearer alternatives.

resolvedEditorialIssues.issue: Pacific ocean versus its adjacent seas
resolvedEditorialIssues.result: The playable phrase explicitly says “the Pacific Ocean or one of its seas.” The programme-scoped Pacific-island phrase has been retired.

resolvedEditorialIssues.issue: Iran under a narrower everyday South Asia reading
resolvedEditorialIssues.result: The broader “In South or West Asia.” phrase avoids that regional-label surprise.

resolvedEditorialIssues.issue: Cuba/Jamaica under a narrower everyday North America reading
resolvedEditorialIssues.result: “In North or Central America, or the Caribbean.” names the areas directly. “In Central America.” is retired rather than requiring players to adopt the M49 scope that includes Mexico.
Only “In the Caribbean.” remains from the three identical Caribbean memberships. There are no identical membership pairs in the final catalog.
Cyprus now has the Asia reveal label in data.js, matching the geographic convention used by its hints.

focusedAssessments.reason: Explicitly allows the Pacific Ocean’s seas; a nonexpert can search its broad rim rather than being caught by an unstated direct-ocean definition.

Two simple constraints in one sentence. “At least three” avoids requiring an exact total, and “sea coast” is understandable basic vocabulary. Landlocked and sea-coast wording need not be treated as opposites for inland seas.
Plain wording, a distinctive relative-size idea and the user’s requested style. Its map-knowledge demand is an optional limitation, not a reason to remove it.
These are simple checks of a letter or two familiar properties. They do not compare first and last letters alphabetically, and they do not ask about repeated letters.
Conventional basic wording. It does not need a long Help definition for shared-island countries.

optionalNotes.finding: The wording is concrete, but a nonexpert needs to know neighbouring countries and their relative land areas. The all-smaller/all-larger clues give a clearer search direction than the mixed-size or one-smaller clues.
optionalNotes.playerUse: All-smaller suggests a large country relative to its immediate surroundings. All-larger suggests a small country between larger ones. Mixed-size and one-smaller are useful checks after a player has candidate countries, and weaker prompts for choosing the first guess.
optionalNotes.suggestion: Keep the requested all-smaller-neighbours fact and these plain comparisons. Future enrichment could add another verified coast or regional fact for affected countries; no wording replacement is required now.

optionalNotes.finding: Some small island countries have exactly the same alternative IDs. Island, ocean coast and island-in-Oceania clues also cover related aspects, so repeated rounds can feel similar even though each clue is usable.
optionalNotes.playerUse: These clues move the search toward small islands or an ocean region. They do not tell a novice much about which island to choose, so the population/area feedback after the first guess remains important.
optionalNotes.suggestion: Accept the current bank. A future source-backed enrichment should add one distinguishable, reusable basic fact for these countries rather than more synonyms for being an island.

strengthContext.assessment: The complete Southern Europe and Asian-island Easy groups can become four-answer shortlists for a player who knows their membership. They remain strong Easy starters rather than unique-country clues; Easy intentionally permits that strength. Medium/Hard now require at least seven declared possible answers under the same current-pool check, while retaining at least four confirmed matches.

partialListCaution.assessment: Four confirmed Easy assignments with an upper bound of fourteen are not an exhaustive four-answer shortlist. No guaranteed-enumeration conclusion is made from this partial list.

strengthContext.interpretation: No capital, iconic landmark, national slogan or uniquely identifying country name is supplied by a starter. Facts with specialised geography still depend on the player’s own knowledge.

declaredPossiblePolicy.appliesTo: Nominal bank eligibility and the actual answer pool after saved exclusions.
declaredPossiblePolicy.assessment: Every Medium/Hard hint now needs at least seven declared possible answers, even when its verified positive list is partial. This closes the policy distinction that allowed a partial clue to fall to a five- or six-answer declared pool late in a journey.
declaredPossiblePolicy.qualification: Declared possible membership includes conservative extras. This editorial review does not certify that every possible extra is a factual match, or independently certify dynamic runtime fairness.

metrics.interpretation: All countries have at least two eligible geography options at their own starting tier before exclusions. Nine to seventeen is the range of reviewed alternatives across allowed tiers; eight to seventeen is the own-tier range. Identical four-example cards do not imply identical gameplay alternatives.

strongExamples.name: India
exampleHints: The name has six letters or fewer.
Population of at least 150 million.
In Asia.
Has at least three land neighbours and a sea coast.
strongExamples.reason: A short name check, a large-population band, Asia and the coast/three-neighbour conjunction provide different ways to get started without a landmark giveaway.

strongExamples.name: Jordan
exampleHints: The name contains O.
Land area from 10,000 to under 100,000 km².
In West Asia.
Has at least three land neighbours and a sea coast.
strongExamples.reason: The letter check, land-area band, West Asia and the coast/three-neighbour conjunction are all plain and usable; the last two describe different aspects.

strongExamples.name: Egypt
exampleHints: The name contains no A.
Population from 50 million to under 150 million.
Has three or four land neighbours.
Has a Mediterranean coast.
strongExamples.reason: A name-letter check, population band, neighbour-count band and familiar Mediterranean coast make a clear mix. A novice can use the sea clue immediately.

strongExamples.name: Brazil
exampleHints: The name has six letters or fewer.
Land area of at least 1,500,000 km².
All its land neighbours are smaller by land area.
Has at least three land neighbours and a sea coast.
strongExamples.reason: The large land-area band and all-smaller-neighbours clue are intuitive ways to think about the country; the coast/three-neighbour option adds a different constraint.

strongExamples.name: Switzerland
exampleHints: The name ends with a consonant.
Land area from 10,000 to under 100,000 km².
Has five or six land neighbours.
In Europe.
strongExamples.reason: The name check, land-area band, neighbour-count band and Europe offer basic alternatives. No specialist neighbour-continent inference is required.

remainingReviewLimits: This is not an independent factual or geographic-membership certification because of my drafting involvement.

The stronger rule was read in the candidate selector, and own-tier eligibility was enumerated with no excluded answers. Dynamic prefix/exclusion coverage, seed distribution and browser gameplay are outside this editorial review.
The minimum of seven for Medium/Hard refers to declared possible matches, including conservative extras; it does not certify seven factual matches.
Knowledge demands vary by player; simple neighbour-area comparisons can still be hard for someone who does not know the local map.
implementationBoundary: Review only. This action creates revised-player-review.json and does not change the bank, game, runtime, tests or other review certificates.
